audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that Zaahen wins 52.07% over 2604 games while the chart gives Yasuo 4 of 7 stages and Zaahen 0 — but both layers agree with each other and with the packet chart, and the mirror deliberately left the sides alone pending a ruling.
audit.why: Flipping rows here without the mirror agreeing would introduce exactly the cross-layer disagreement the regression check blocks. The imbalance is a champion-level ruling, not a per-matchup guess.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 6 and late-game text gave no cooldown for Last Breath and told you to hold your R as 'a peel/anti-dash tool' and to 'punish his dash-in' with it.
audit.why: Last Breath is 70/50/30s — at rank 3 it is back before most fights reset, which changes how you spend a 110-second R. And Zaahen's R has no CC: it damages and heals, so it cannot peel or interrupt a dash.
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text, late, dontsFull[1].d and breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with the real cooldown and the real effect.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page is built on a Wind Wall thesis: nine fields tell you to bait or respect the wall before you poke or engage. None of Zaahen's abilities carries the projectile flag — Riot's text describes an empowered melee double-slash, a directional stab-and-pull, a dash-and-slice and a downward stab. Wind Wall blocks nothing you cast. Worse, the actual decisive interaction was absent: both your Q recast and your W knock up, and Last Breath blinks to an airborne champion.
audit.why: Spending the trade on baiting a 25-second wall that was never going to matter is a losing pattern, while handing him a free knock-up at 6 is how the lane is actually lost. Yasuo's real early edge is Steel Tempest's 475 range on a 4s cooldown plus E dashes off minions.
audit.corrected: whys[1], whys[2], whys[4], spikes[0], spikes[2], spikes[3], early, mid, late, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], all three dos and all three donts rewritten around range, tempo and the airborne rule.

edits.before: Yasuo's early edge is his Wind Wall (W) and Steel Tempest (Q) poke — he sits behind minions, pokes your low-range Q Darkin Glaive trades, and blocks your engage-tell with Wind Wall. edits.after: Yasuo's early edge is Steel Tempest (Q, 4s, 475 range) and Sweeping Blade (E) off the minions — he pokes from outside your reach and resets spacing before you can answer. Wind Wall blocks projectiles and you cast none, so trade on his Q cooldown instead of wasting turns baiting the wall.

edits.before: Yasuo's first-item power (Immortal Shield-broken IE/crit spike) plus his passive shield and double-crit lets him out-trade you on cooldown. Play the wave to deny his E dashes off minions and only commit when Wind Wall is down.
edits.after: Yasuo's first-item crit spike plus the passive shield lets him out-trade you on cooldown. Play the wave to deny his E dashes off minions, and stop routing around Wind Wall — your slash, your pull and your dash all pass straight through it.

edits.before: Two items in, Yasuo's mobility and Wind Wall make him a persistent duel and pick threat; your telegraphed E is easy for him to dodge or wall. Hold R Final Retribution as a peel/anti-dash tool and win through grouping, not sidelane duels.
edits.after: Two items in, Yasuo's mobility makes him a persistent duel and pick threat, and his E leaves your dash behind. Your R deals damage and heals but interrupts nothing, so spend it inside the fight and win through grouping, not sidelane duels.

edits.before: Level 1-2 is even farming, but Yasuo out-ranges your Q trades with Steel Tempest and can already deny your poke with Wind Wall, so don't force it. Keep the wave neutral, deny his early tornado stacks by not clumping, and hold E Golden Onslaught rather than dashing into a wall.
edits.after: Level 1-2 is even farming, but Steel Tempest outranges your trades at 475 on a 4-second cooldown, so don't force it. Keep the wave neutral, deny his tornado stacks by never standing in line with your own minions, and hold your dash for his step-in rather than spending it first.

edits.before: This is Yasuo's window and why the chart is his: his Wind Wall neutralises your Q Darkin Glaive poke and telegraphs your E engage, while his E-through-minions mobility lets him pick trade angles and stack tornado for a knock-up all-in. Respect the wall, keep minions between you, and never commit E into a clean knock-up setup.
edits.after: This is Yasuo's window and why the chart is his: Steel Tempest outranges your trades on a 4-second cooldown and his E-through-minions mobility lets him choose every angle and stack tornado for a knock-up all-in. The wall is not your problem — his spacing is — so trade on his Q timer and never hand him a free airborne at 6.

edits.before: With items Yasuo's crit, shield passive and mobility make him a slippery duelist who dodges or walls your engage. Don't chase in the sidelane — group, hold R Final Retribution to punish his dash-in, and let your team apply the knock-up he fears.
edits.after: With items Yasuo's crit, shield passive and mobility make him a slippery duelist who simply dashes out of your engage. Don't chase in the sidelane — group, hold your R for the damage and heal once he commits, and stop handing him free airborne targets.
